verdict.rationale: Better Auth's own docs show it can act as an OAuth authorization server: the MCP plugin makes the app an authorization server and protected resource for MCP clients, and the Device Authorization plugin implements RFC 8628 code issuance and approval. Community comments corroborate that it can act as an identity provider and OIDC/SSO provider. However, the documented authorization-server role is scoped to MCP clients and device flows rather than general third-party 'Sign in with my app' clients. Missing for 10: first-party docs for a general OAuth/OIDC provider (client registration, authorization-code flow, consent, token and userinfo endpoints for arbitrary third-party apps), and hands-on corroboration of issuing tokens to external clients.

support.subject: As a developer, I can turn my own application into an OAuth provider that issues tokens to third-party clients ("Sign in with my app")

citations.quote: The **MCP** plugin lets your app act as an OAuth authorization server and protected resource for [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) clients.
The Device Authorization plugin implements the code issuance and approval flow from the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant
acting as an identity provider and OIDC/SSO provider
